newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end tad higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end tad higher.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed a shade higher Friday weathering the impact of options expirations, dealers said.
"Optimism on Wall Street helped the bolsa soak up selling at the end of a short-covering wave," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index edged up 0.3 percent to 628, boosting gains this week to 4.6 percent. But traders forecast some profit taking.
"We digested options-related selling today but we could now be heading for a correction," Bonanno said.
He predicted the MerVal might ease to 613 by the end of next week, "which would be only a normal correction considering that liquidity is always tighter in the last days of the year."
Analysts said bolsa volume would shrink next week but investors would continue to track movements in New York, especially the long bond yield.

"The market will probably turn more selective in the next few days, because several stocks including those listed abroad as ADRs have already reached resistance levels," said Jose Napoli at traders Ignoto y Napoli.
The broad market rose 0.2 percent in the session, with winners overtaking losers 29 to 26 and 18 stocks closing flat.
Floor volume swelled to 29.7 million pesos from 26 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals plummeted to 68.4 million pesos from 106.3 million Thursday.
Best main-tier performers were construction stock Polledo, which jumped 3.0 percent, and holding companies Comercial del Plata and Cresud, up 2.0 percent and 1.8 percent respectively.
Losers were led by oil firm Sol Petroleo and petrochemical concern Ipako, off 6.8 percent and 2.5 percent each.
